triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The module carried `rules: []` with `status: deferred`, so HTS 9903.05.39's operative clause — that EU-origin articles whose column-1 ad valorem rate is less than 10 percent take a 10% rate, except for goods described in headings 9903.05.85–9903.05.92 and 9903.05.97 — was not represented in the encoding at all.
triage.triage_notes: Read the provision through the pinned resolver: source text is "articles the product of a member state of the European Union, with an ad valorem (or ad valorem equivalent) rate of duty under column 1 less than 10 percent" with "Rates of duty (1-General): 10%" / "(1-Special): 10%", so the added strict `<` against a 0.10 threshold and the 0.10 floor rate match the source; the resolver reported fix_time_corpus_match=provision_file_absent_at_corpus_ref and fell back to release us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union, so the text is from a later release than the toolchain corpus ref. The fix bundles three things: (a) the substantive encoding of the missing clause, (b) a rename of every export to a `_floor_` infix, which is what cleared the stated deferral reason ("Generated rule used a local name that collides with a sibling RuleSpec export") and is mechanical, and (c) the same en-dash summary repair as the rest of the chunk; it also switches module.source_verification to plural `corpus_citation_paths` adding us/statute/hts/9903.05.38 to ground the else-branch of the two rate rules on the sibling heading. A companion test file us/policies/usitc/us-tariff-duty/overlays/section-301/forced-labor-eu-9903-05-39.test.yaml was added in the same commit (only the five floor headings and the composition got tests). Caveat for the reviewer: the pre-fix module self-declared the gap via `deferred_outputs`/`status: deferred` rather than encoding a wrong formula, so if the corpus is meant to hold only silently-wrong meanings this belongs at 'unclear'; I kept 'fidelity' because the rubric treats added source-required coverage as unrepresented_clause and the maintainers treated the omission as a review blocker. PR #1196 body records no reviews or review comments in the bundle (0 reviews, 0 review comments, 0 issue comments), so the commit message is the only stated reason.
triage.verifier_justification: The pre-fix file encoded nothing at all — it was a machine-declared stub (`rules: []`, `module.status: deferred`) whose three `deferred_outputs` entries each name the missing output and state the reason, the first being an encoder namespace problem ("Generated rule used a local name that collides with a sibling RuleSpec export"), with the other two deferred only as dependents of it. Under the rubric a fidelity defect is "an encoded meaning that disagrees with the cited source text"; here no formula, parameter, version, date, input/output or scope asserted anything that the source contradicts, so the fix supplies coverage the module explicitly disclaimed rather than repairing a clause missing from a working encoding. That the repair renames the blocked output to the collision-free `forced_labor_eu_floor_heading_applies` confirms the gap's cause was a pipeline/naming block, not a misreading of HTS 9903.05.39. Git history also shows the stub was created by the immediate parent commit 4dfebb74e in the same PR (#1196) and drained in this intra-PR repair round, so no incorrect encoded meaning ever existed as a shipped state.
triage.verifier_notes: Post-fix encoding is itself faithful (checked against the pinned release, us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union, provision text: "Except for products described in headings 9903.05.85–9903.05.92 and 9903.05.97, articles the product of a member state of the European Union, with an ad valorem (or ad valorem equivalent) rate of duty under column 1 less than 10 percent... Rates of duty (1-General): 10%"), so strict `<`, the 0.10 threshold, the 0.10 rate and both exception carve-outs all match — but that speaks to the quality of the added encoding, not to the pre-state being wrong. Verbatim deferral reason from the diff (line-wrapped in the file): "-    reason: Generated rule used a local name that collides with a sibling RuleSpec" / "-      export. This output is deferred until it can be encoded with a semantic branch-specific" / "-      name without creating ambiguous sibling imports." PR #1196 carries zero reviews, review comments, or issue comments in the bundle, so the only "review blocker" evidence is the commit author's own summary line, which is self-reported. Residual uncertainty for the curator: if this corpus's policy is that a declared deferral leaving a cited provision unrepresented counts as a fidelity gap, then the first reader's kind (unrepresented_clause) is the right fallback and the verdict would be confirmed; I read the rubric's carve-out ("new outputs... or scope the module never claimed is not a defect") as controlling because `deferred_outputs` enumerates precisely the outputs never claimed. Secondary changes in the same diff are provenance-only: hyphen→en-dash in the summary heading range, `corpus_citation_path` → `corpus_citation_paths` (adding us/statute/hts/9903.05.38 for the complement branch), and removal of an empty `imports:` key.
